question_bank.stem: A frontier model loses performance on law questions after the last month of training. What data diagnostic should be checked first?

options.text: Whether the law domain became underrepresented in recent data
Whether the first convolutional filter detects edges
Whether the reward model prefers answer A over answer B
Whether the softmax probability for dog is post-normalized

question_bank.rationale: The lecture says domain proportions matter and that lower representation in a domain can lead to a performance drop in that domain.

distractor_rationales.B: Convolutional edge filters are unrelated to domain-specific frontier-model performance.
distractor_rationales.C: Reward-model preference is an RLHF topic, not this data-distribution diagnostic.
distractor_rationales.D: Dog softmax is from saliency-map discussion, not law-domain data drift.

source_ref.evidence_span: the performance of the model on that domain

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows The Pile-style data-domain distribution chart with domains such as law, Stack Exchange, and GitHub.

question_bank.stem: The lecture compares stable data-domain sampling to replay memory because both aim to maintain what property during training?

options.text: Stable frequencies of important examples or domains across training portions
Identical softmax values for every output class
A single selected expert for every batch
A cropped receptive field for every activation

question_bank.rationale: The instructor connects replay-memory-style sampling methods to keeping domain frequencies stable across different training portions.

distractor_rationales.B: The goal is not equal softmax values.
distractor_rationales.C: A single expert for every batch is a routing failure, not a sampling goal.
distractor_rationales.D: Receptive-field cropping is a CNN interpretation method.

source_ref.evidence_span: the frequency of data domain the same at different portions

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows The Pile-style data-domain distribution chart with domains such as law, Stack Exchange, and GitHub.

question_bank.stem: Token statistics can diagnose task regressions because changes in important token frequencies may cause what outcome?

options.text: Worse performance on tasks that rely on those tokens
Guaranteed benchmark decontamination without held-out data
A class activation map with better localization

question_bank.rationale: The lecture gives token frequency changes as a signal that can lead to worse performance, such as with math-related tokens.

distractor_rationales.B: Token statistics do not by themselves repair contaminated benchmarks.
distractor_rationales.C: Pooling switches are CNN reconstruction metadata.
distractor_rationales.D: CAM localization is a separate CNN attribution method.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows token-distribution diagnostics and anomalous token-frequency shifts.

question_bank.stem: Synthetic data can help augmentation, but the lecture warns against overusing cheap synthetic data in one domain because it can do what?

options.text: Distort token frequencies and lower performance elsewhere
Force all experts to be load balanced automatically
Convert data-domain checks into saliency maps

question_bank.rationale: The Q&A warns that generated synthetic data may change token frequencies and lower performance on the rest of the distribution.

distractor_rationales.B: Synthetic data does not automatically fix MoE load balancing.
distractor_rationales.C: Synthetic data does not make benchmark contamination impossible.
distractor_rationales.D: Data-domain checks do not become CNN saliency maps.

source_ref.evidence_span: and lowers the performance on the rest

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows token-distribution diagnostics and anomalous token-frequency shifts.
